fields.description: The engine/discipline this snapshot covers (e.g. 'Electrical'). Retention is per-discipline: the newest 10 are kept.
fields.label: Discipline

fields.description: Monotonic per discipline, starting at 1. Assigned at write time as (max existing for this discipline) + 1; it is NOT reused after a prune, so a version number always identifies one snapshot for the life of the site.
fields.label: Version

fields.description: The whole loader-ready asset, EXACTLY as the export handed it to the user. LONG TEXT, not JSON, and that is deliberate: the payload is an opaque serialised artefact whose value is byte-fidelity (a snapshot exists to be restored), so Frappe must never hydrate and re-serialise it. It also sidesteps the list-valued-JSON wall that forces Pricing Workbook Version's prune to use a raw frappe.db.delete.
fields.label: Payload

fields.description: The session user who took the export (admin-gated).
fields.label: Taken By

fields.description: The import_batch the exported rows belonged to -- the join back to the catalog rows this snapshot describes. Blank if the discipline held no active rows.
fields.label: Import Batch

fields.description: Item count in the payload -- a cheap integrity check that does not require parsing it.
fields.label: Item Count

fields.description: Config count in the payload -- the second half of the same cheap integrity check.
fields.label: Config Count
